title: Best Hanging Dehumidifier (2026): Bags & Hanging Kits
h1: The Best Hanging Dehumidifiers, From Closet Bags to Crawl-Space Units
dek: Off the floor and out of the way: hanging moisture bags for closets and cars, and suspended dehumidifiers for crawl spaces.
description: The best hanging dehumidifier for closets, cars and crawl spaces: hanging dehumidifier bags, a reusable option and the Aprilaire 5822 hanging kit, explained.
intro: A **hanging dehumidifier** means two very different things depending on who's searching. For most people, it's a moisture-absorbing bag or canister that hooks over a closet rod, a garage shelf or a car's coat hook. For homeowners with a sealed crawl space or a cramped basement, it's a full-size dehumidifier suspended from the floor joists on a hanging kit, so it sits above the vapor barrier instead of on it.

We cover both here. For the passive options, we compared absorbent type, how long each lasts, whether it's reusable and how it handles the collected water. For suspended units, we looked at rated capacity, coverage, drainage, warranty and which hanging kits the manufacturer actually supports. Then we read owner reviews for leaks, early failures and installation headaches.
topPicksLead: For closets, the **DampRid Hanging Moisture Absorber** is the easiest hanging dehumidifier to start with; for crawl spaces, the **Aprilaire E070** paired with Aprilaire's 5822 hanging kit is our top suspended pick.

products.name: DampRid Hanging Moisture Absorber
pros: Hooks over a closet rod, using no shelf space
Rated to last up to 60 days
Sealed bag with a clear chamber for collected water
products.whyWeLoveIt: This is the hanging dehumidifier bag most people picture, and for good reason: it hangs between your clothes, collects water in a see-through pocket at the bottom and goes in the trash in one piece when it's full. It's the simplest way to find out whether a closet has a humidity problem at all.
products.performance: DampRid rates its hanging bags for up to 60 days, depending on how humid the space is. Calcium chloride crystals pull moisture from the air and turn it into brine that drains into the sealed lower pouch. DampRid says not to cut the bag open; when the liquid reaches the fill line, toss it whole. Compare formats in our [best moisture absorber](/best/best-moisture-absorber/) guide.

specs.Mounting: Hangs from a rod or hook

products.name: Eva-Dry E-500 Renewable Dehumidifier
pros: Renewable silica gel — no bags to rebuy
Color indicator shows when it needs recharging
cons: Must be plugged in to recharge
Passive, so a very damp closet can outpace it
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you'd rather not throw away a bag every two months, the E-500 is the reusable alternative. It hangs between garments, soaks up moisture with silica gel, and when the crystals change color you plug it in to dry them out and hang it right back up.
products.performance: Eva-Dry rates it for spaces of about 500 cubic feet, which suits a walk-in closet or a large cabinet. Because the moisture stays locked in the gel rather than pooling as liquid, there's nothing to leak onto clothes or shoes. Recharging takes an overnight plug-in, and owners report years of reuse. More options are in our [rechargeable dehumidifier](/best/best-rechargeable-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: The two categories don't overlap. A bag won't touch a damp crawl space, and a 70-pint machine is absurd in a coat closet. Decide which problem you're solving first.

We don't run a test lab. For bags and canisters, we compare the manufacturer's rated lifespan and space coverage, how the collected water is contained, and owner reports of leaks and how quickly products fill in real closets. For suspended units, we use AHAM capacity ratings, coverage, warranty terms and the manufacturer's own list of supported hanging kits, then check owner and installer feedback and the CPSC recall database.

sections.heading: What to look for in a hanging dehumidifier

items.label: Leak-proof containment
items.text: Calcium chloride brine can stain fabric and corrode metal. Choose sealed bags with a separate collection chamber, and hang them where a drip won't land on anything valuable.

items.label: Reusable vs. disposable
items.text: Disposable bags are cheapest to start; a rechargeable unit costs more up front but pays off over a few seasons.

items.label: The right space
items.text: Passive hangers suit enclosed spaces like closets and cars. A room that stays damp needs an electric dehumidifier; see our [closet dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-closet/) picks for both.

items.label: A manufacturer-supported hanging kit
items.text: For crawl-space units, use the hanger the maker designs for the model rather than improvised straps, and confirm the model is on its compatibility list.

items.label: A drainage plan
items.text: Suspended units still need a gravity line or condensate pump. Map the route before you lift the unit into place.

blocks.text: The **Aprilaire 5822 dehumidifier hanging kit** is a strap-and-bracket set for suspending an Aprilaire dehumidifier from floor joists. Retailers consistently list it for the E070, E080 and E100; some also list the E130 and older 1800-series models, so check your manual or Aprilaire's parts list before ordering.

items: It keeps the unit off the vapor barrier, so it can't puncture or wear through it.
It stays above any water that seeps in during a storm.
It frees floor space in a tight crawl and makes filter checks easier from the hatch.
Less dust and debris reach the intake at joist height.
Anchor into solid framing, following the kit's instructions for spacing.
Hang the unit as level as the manual specifies so the condensate drains properly.
Leave clearance around the intake, exhaust and filter door.
Run the drain line with a continuous downward slope, or add a condensate pump.
Plug into a dedicated, GFCI-protected outlet where local code requires it.

sections.heading: Dehumidifier bags for cars, bathrooms and basements

blocks.text: Hanging bags are a closet tool first. In other spaces, they work better in some places than others:

items: **Cars:** A calcium chloride bag that tips over can leak brine onto upholstery. Sealed silica-gel bags are a safer car dehumidifier bag; our [car dehumidifier guide](/best/best-car-dehumidifier/) has picks.
**Bathrooms:** Shower steam fills bags fast. An exhaust fan does the real work; for a windowless bathroom see our [bathroom dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-bathroom/) picks.
**Basements:** Bags are far too small for a basement. Even a modest one needs an electric dehumidifier; start with our [basement guide](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-basement/).

blocks.title: Handle the brine carefully
blocks.text: Calcium chloride liquid irritates skin and eyes and corrodes metal. Keep bags away from children and pets, don't cut them open, and dispose of them as the package directs.

For a damp closet, start with the **DampRid Hanging Moisture Absorber**, and switch to the reusable **Eva-Dry E-500** if you're tired of replacing bags. For a crawl space, the **Aprilaire E070** on Aprilaire's 5822 hanging kit keeps the machine off the vapor barrier and out of harm's way, while the **Aprilaire E100** suits basements and larger spaces that need whole-house capacity.

faqs.q: What is the Aprilaire 5822 hanging kit?
faqs.a: It's Aprilaire's strap-and-bracket kit for suspending its dehumidifiers from floor joists. Retailers consistently list it for the E070, E080 and E100; some also include the E130 and older 1800-series units, so confirm compatibility in your manual.
Yes, in small, enclosed spaces like closets and lockers. Calcium chloride bags pull a noticeable amount of water from the air over several weeks. They can't dry an open room or a basement.

faqs.q: Are reusable dehumidifier bags better than disposable ones?
faqs.a: Over time, usually. Rechargeable silica-gel units like the Eva-Dry E-500 cost more up front but last for years and don't produce liquid brine. Disposable calcium chloride bags are cheaper to start and need no outlet.

faqs.q: Can I use dehumidifier bags in a car?
faqs.a: Yes, but choose sealed silica-gel bags over calcium chloride ones, which can leak corrosive brine if they tip or get crushed. Recharge silica bags at home when their indicator changes color.

faqs.q: How long does a hanging dehumidifier bag last?
faqs.a: DampRid rates its hanging bags for up to 60 days. In a very humid closet or bathroom, expect them to fill sooner.

faqs.q: Can you hang a crawl-space dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Many can, using the manufacturer's hanging kit. Hanging keeps the unit off the vapor barrier and above any water. Follow the kit's instructions, keep the unit level and give the drain line a continuous slope.
